solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Diverts variety acts with half of recording?

parts.note: turns are acts in a variety show
a single record has two sides, the A-side being one half of it

explanation.surface: Someone redirects a variety show's acts to fill half of a record.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-side is the main track of a two-sided single, so it is half of the recording.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something aside is to deflect it from its course, which is what diverting means.

clue.text: Leader leaves men in dry shelter

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened word men goes inside the abbreviation for dry

parts.note: TT means teetotal, dry

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, leaves the word men

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A boss walks out on the men in a teetotal refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry means teetotal here, abbreviated TT, not lacking moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent is a portable canvas shelter.

clue.text: Turned back, being hurt again?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wound back, as a tape is
second meaning: ..., read as ..., given a wound once more

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second reading stretches the word to mean wounded again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rewound tape or clock has been wound back, and someone injured a second time could be called re-wounded.

clue.text: Mr Ed supporting son who's standing provokingly?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath, so the son comes under the horse

parts.note: Mister Ed was the talking horse of a 1960s American TV sitcom

explanation.surface: A TV horse props up a boy who is acting provocatively.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the supporting letter sits below, so S comes before the rest when read.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalking horse is a candidate who stands in a leadership contest to provoke a challenge for someone else.

clue.text: Nosily picks up small coins

parts.note: cents are small coins

explanation.surface: Someone nosy gathers loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nosily' suggests prying, but it means by nose: smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To scent something is to pick up its smell through the nose.

clue.text: Face villain failing to initiate exchange

parts.note: a dial is a clock face

indicators.note: failing to initiate means the word does not start, losing its first letter

parts.note: a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A villain confronted fails to start a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is an exchange of views or conversation between people.

clue.text: Twelve back-to-back refusals

parts.note: no is a refusal; two of them are needed here

indicators.note: back to back means the second refusal faces the other way, so it is written backwards against the first

explanation.surface: Someone says no a dozen times in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock midday, so the number stands for the time.

clue.text: Strikers on team? Not likely!

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A footballer scoffs at the idea of the forwards joining the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' and 'team' suggest football, but strikers here are workers out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: An outside chance is a slim one, so outside here means improbable.

clue.text: Breeder runs many dodgy houses I hesitate to say

indicators.note: houses means the jumbled letters hold the next piece inside them
dodgy means unsound, so the letters of runs many are rearranged

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A breeder hesitantly admits to running many shady houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breeder' suggests animals, but a nurseryman breeds plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseryman raises and breeds plants for sale.

clue.text: Innovative artists in revolutionary city flourish

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning over, so the city's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Wen, or Great Wen, is Cobbett's old nickname for London
to wave something is to flourish it

explanation.surface: Avant-garde artists thrive in a city that has had a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wen is London, from William Cobbett's 'Great Wen', a city swollen like a cyst.
explanation.definitionFit: New Wave names a movement of innovative film-makers and musicians breaking with convention.

clue.text: One grazing animals gets air exercising

indicators.note: exercising puts the letters of gets air through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal out to graze gets fresh air while exercising.
explanation.walkthrough: To agist is to take in livestock to graze for payment; in the New Forest an agister is the official overseeing the free-roaming animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An agister is a person who pastures other people's livestock, so he is the one grazing them.

clue.text: Forcibly conditioned with art, not love?

definitions.text: Forcibly conditioned with art, not love?

indicators.note: forcibly means the letters are wrenched into a new order
not means the next letter is excluded from the mix

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Someone has been brainwashed through art rather than affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CONDITIONED and ART, remove one O (love), and rearrange; the whole clue also describes brainwashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoctrinated means taught to accept beliefs uncritically, a kind of forcible conditioning of the mind.

clue.text: Vagrant blacked out a lot

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters of blacked out wander into another order

explanation.surface: A tramp has drunk so much he passed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vagrant' reads as a noun for the person who blacked out, but it is an adjective signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucketload is an informal word for a great quantity.

clue.text: Wrath in country deprived of land

indicators.note: deprived of means losing something, here the word land

parts.note: Ireland is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation stripped of its territory is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary synonym for anger or wrath.

clue.text: Pals inspiring another's schemes

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the pals take the next word inside

parts.note: mates are pals
another pal: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Friends encourage someone else's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so a china is another pal.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to plot or devise intrigues, so machinates means plots or schemes.

clue.text: Forest close to airport burning

parts.note: the Forest of Arden, setting of As You Like It

indicators.note: close here means the end, so only the last letter of airport counts

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A forest fire rages near an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, figuratively burning with feeling; literally it once meant on fire.

clue.text: Faithful friend concealing Conservative party's latest fraudulence

indicators.note: concealing means the friend holds the next letter inside

parts.note: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends, a faith

indicators.note: latest means the final letter

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A loyal friend covers up a Tory party's recent dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: Friend with a capital F, as Quakers call themselves, is hidden behind 'Faithful friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quackery is the fraudulent practice of a charlatan, so it amounts to fraudulence.

clue.text: Rugby player hits low note, roughly a fortnightly occurrence

parts.note: a half, such as a scrum half or fly half, is a rugby back
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A rugby player belts out a deep note every couple of weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low note' looks like a bass sound, but low is the cow's moo.
explanation.definitionFit: A half moon appears at first and last quarter, about once every two weeks.

clue.text: Butt from corner disposed of outside area

parts.note: to corner a market is to hog it

indicators.note: outside means the first word goes round the next letter

parts.note: shed means got rid of

explanation.surface: A cigarette end from a street corner is binned outside a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' looks like a cigarette end but is a large cask.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt and a hogshead are both large casks for wine or beer.

clue.text: Pioneering Russian paper set up in advance

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed paper sits inside the word for advance

parts.note: to gain is to advance

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A Russian newspaper is prepared ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means written upwards, which reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin was the Soviet cosmonaut who became the first human in space in 1961.

clue.text: Ships seized by war-mad admiral?

indicators.note: seized by means held within the following words

explanation.surface: A warlike admiral takes command of a fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: A barrister recalled eponymous heroine before 6 once

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: KC is King's Counsel, a senior barrister
Emma is the heroine who gives her name to Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: A lawyer remembers a famous heroine before a sixth chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 refers to the answer at 6 across, NOON; ack emma was the old military signallers' word for a.m.
explanation.definitionFit: In the First World War signalling alphabet A was ack and M emma, so ack emma meant a.m., the morning.

clue.text: I'm off to appraise housing development

indicators.note: off means the letters of I'm are taken away

parts.note: to estimate is to appraise
taken as written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A surveyor leaves to value a new housing scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm off' reads as someone departing, but it removes IM from ESTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a planned development of homes built together.

clue.text: Last of seamen to swig drink

indicators.note: last of applies to each of the three words that follow, taking their final letters

explanation.surface: The last sailor knocks back a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of' reads as applying only to seamen, but it takes the end of each of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nog is a strong ale, also short for eggnog, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Nonconformists waste nothing they say

parts.note: refuse is waste or rubbish

indicators.note: they say means the next word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Dissenters claim nothing is wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuseniks were Soviet Jews refused emigration; the term now covers anyone who refuses to conform.

clue.text: My investment company's base

parts.note: an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a British tax-free savings investment

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, the last letter

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone shows off the base of their investment firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: My! and I say! are both exclamations expressing surprise.

clue.text: Missile turned over HQ, crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the reversed letters straddle the river
turned means read backwards

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a depot is a headquarters

explanation.surface: A missile turned and flew over headquarters, across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' reads as one phrase, but over is the cricket O and only 'turned' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile.

clue.text: Not always where top columnists work?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: on the staff of The Times newspaper, home of leading columnists

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the setter's nod to the paper the puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, and read literally places a writer at The Times newspaper.

clue.text: Celebrated dynasty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: praised in song, past participle of sing
second meaning: the Chinese dynasty that ruled from 960 to 1279, also spelt Song

explanation.definitionFit: Something sung is praised or extolled, and Sung is also the name of an imperial Chinese ruling house.

clue.text: Provocative church featured in local chronicle

indicators.note: featured in means placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: a local is a pub, an inn
CE is the Church of England
a diary is a daily chronicle

explanation.surface: An inflammatory church features in the local newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local chronicle' looks like a parish paper, but local is the pub, as Britons call their nearest one.
explanation.definitionFit: An incendiary remark is inflammatory, deliberately provocative.
